chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Abi Basir, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The donors are three: God the Donor; the one who donates from his property; and the one who strives in that [matter], [is considered] a donor.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of donors mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) categorizing donors into three tiers: God as the ultimate source, the individual giving from their wealth, and the facilitator who strives in the act. This triad highlights the Shia emphasis on *sabr* and effort in charity, where the 'saa’i' (striver) shares in the reward of the giver, reflecting the principle that intent and facilitation are integral to the spiritual economy of giving. This classification underscores the interconnectedness of divine grace and human agency in charitable acts.
